probes.title: One phone number, many identities
probes.goal: Turn one SIM into many 'verified people', each with its own entry.
probes.expected: all five count as the same one person
probes.result: 5 identities created from one phone number
probes.why: The phone number is reduced to digits before it becomes an identity, and codes per phone are capped.

probes.title: Guess someone's login code
probes.goal: Take over a victim's account by trying codes until one fits (only 1,000,000 exist).
probes.move: 12 wrong guesses from 12 different addresses, then the right code
probes.expected: the code is destroyed after a few wrong guesses
probes.result: after 12 wrong guesses the correct code was ACCEPTED (unlimited guesses!)
probes.why: 5 wrong guesses kill the code; the owner must request a new one.

probes.title: Spam login codes at one number
probes.goal: Make the site send 1,000s of SMS to one number (costs money, harasses the owner).
probes.move: Ask for a code for the same number 8 times in a row
probes.expected: only a few are sent, the rest are refused (429)
probes.why: Max 3 codes per number per 10 minutes.

probes.title: Guess the admin password
probes.goal: Get into the admin screens by trying passwords.
probes.move: 9 wrong passwords in a row from one address
probes.expected: the address is locked out after a few tries
probes.result: 0 of 9 attempts were locked out (the rest were told 'wrong password')
probes.why: 5 wrong passwords per address locks it for 5 minutes. Use a strong ADMIN_PASSWORD (the server refuses demo secrets outside demo mode).

probes.title: Send enormous requests
probes.goal: Exhaust the server's memory with huge requests.
probes.move: A 300 KB 'ticket' (a real one is ~0.5 KB)
probes.expected: refused at the door without being read
probes.why: Bodies over 64 KB are refused by the gateway and again by the server.

probes.title: Hijack someone's retry key
probes.goal: Break an honest person's safe-retry so they lose their receipt (or get someone else's).
probes.move: Use the same Idempotency-Key as the victim, with the attacker's own valid ticket
probes.expected: the victim's retry still returns the victim's own receipt
probes.result: victim retry: HTTP 409, own receipt returned=False; attacker's call: HTTP 200
probes.why: A retry key only counts together with its own ticket, so keys can't collide across people.

probes.title: Use a ticket from a different sale
probes.goal: Re-use a valid ticket in another sale to enter twice.
probes.move: Take a signed ticket from sale A to sale B
probes.expected: rejected (each sale has its own key)
probes.why: Each sale signs with its own key.

probes.title: Fake a login
probes.goal: Skip verification by presenting a login card you wrote yourself (no signature).
probes.why: Only the server's signature is accepted.

probes.title: Forge an admin login with the demo secret
probes.goal: Become admin by signing a token with the secret printed in the demo config.
probes.result: HTTP 200 (this demo is running with the demo secret, so it works HERE; a real deployment cannot start with it)
probes.why: Outside demo mode the server refuses to start with the demo admin password, JWT secret or test key.

probes.title: Peek at the secret draw seed early
probes.goal: Learn the draw's randomness before entering, then craft a ticket that is sure to win.
probes.move: Read the public sale page while it is open
probes.expected: the seed is not published until after the list is sealed
probes.result: only the seed's fingerprint is public
probes.why: The seed is committed (hash) up front and revealed only after the list is sealed.

probes.title: Watch tier crowding, then pounce
probes.goal: Wait until the last second, see which tier has the best odds, and enter that one.
probes.move: Read the public numbers while the sale is open
probes.expected: no live entry counts are public during the sale
probes.result: no public per-tier entry counts during the sale
probes.why: Entry counts appear only after the list is sealed.

probes.title: Ask for a second ticket in another tier
probes.goal: Double the chances by getting one ticket per tier.
probes.move: Same person asks for a gold ticket, then a general one
probes.expected: second request refused (one ticket per person per sale)
probes.why: One ticket per verified person per sale, whatever the tier.

probes.title: Lie about your internet address
probes.goal: Send unlimited requests by inventing a new address in the headers each time.
probes.move: 80 fast requests, each claiming a different address header
probes.expected: the gateway ignores the claims and slows the real address
probes.why: The gateway overwrites the address header with the real one.

probes.title: Switch tier at the last moment
probes.goal: Pick the tier after seeing the crowd.
probes.move: Ticket requested for Gold, entered as General
probes.expected: allowed on purpose (the ticket doesn't carry a tier, so nobody can tell), harmless because crowding is hidden
probes.why: A blind signature cannot carry the tier; see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.
